assumptions.note: ASSUMPTIONS, not measurements: per-call token counts, prices and latency for an LLM agent run. Edit jitd/bench.py to change them. Agent strategies are assumed correct on every run (generous to the baselines).

definitions.silent_error: A ledger entry was POSTED that differs from the independent oracle (or was posted when the oracle says a human must review). Held, halted and crashed runs are not silent.
definitions.silent_error_rate: silent_error / post-onset runs. Lower is better.
definitions.needs_protection: A post-onset run where unguarded naive replay does not produce the oracle-correct posted entry (wrong entry, entry that should not exist, or a crash).
definitions.detection_rate: Share of needs_protection runs the strategy handled: correct entry posted (recovered), or correctly blocked/held. Higher is better.
definitions.false_block: A run where naive replay was correct (so no protection was needed) but the strategy halted or held it. Held-for-review counts: it costs an operator.
definitions.false_block_rate: false_block / post-onset runs where naive replay is correct.
definitions.localization: On the first halted/flagged run of a stream: the top-ranked hypothesis names the scenario's true fault location (or correctly says 'business exception').
definitions.repair: A repair is accepted only if every drift case and regression case passes in an isolated validation run and the oracle agrees.

caveats: Mock provider authored by the same team as the contracts; held-out scenarios were not used to set thresholds but this is not an external benchmark.
Agent baselines are modelled, not run, and assumed correct.
Repair uses the deterministic synthesizer; Nemotron-assisted repair is not measured here.
Repair validation here runs in-process (same function as the isolated worker).

Process note: the golden corpus used for mining was raised from 60 to 400 runs after false positives appeared on the dev 'clean' scenario (a tail-estimation problem); the heldout scenarios were visible in that same run. The x3 range margin and 0.01 tolerance were never changed.
JIT-D holds legitimately huge invoices for review (see big_invoice): magnitude warnings cannot tell a whale invoice from a unit shift on a single run.
